BiblicalUsage: Zuw is a relative word — 'which,' 'whom,' 'that' — the word that ties a person to what God has done for them. Moses sings of the people 'whom thou hast redeemed,' Isaiah speaks of the people 'which I have formed for myself,' and the psalmist hears God say, 'I will instruct thee' — the one whom He guides. It is a small word that holds a people to their God.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that 'whom' is the word of belonging: I am the one He redeemed, the one He formed, the one He guides.
